status_changes.quote: Decision Authority confirms and adopts R-81 through R-85 without amendment.
THESE FIVE ARE THEREFORE PREPARED RULINGS AWAITING ADOPTION
status_changes.note: A mentions this change in a note but omits it from status_changes although M_chain requires every change to be attributed; it is attributable, so the condition still holds

circular_values.derivation: from R-89's PREPARED marker plus R-86's rule 'Any future ruling issued by the ARB Chief remains PREPARED, NOT ADOPTED, until the Decision Authority acts on it' plus the precedent that a PREPARED ruling's effect does not hold
circular_values.why_circular: force derived from status (and status from issuer), then used to test M_status (consistent pair), M_issuer (deciding pair) and M_adopter (deciding pair). No row states R-89's force; 'WP-4C-1 ... is AUTHORIZED' is authorization of a slice, not force.
issuer -> status -> force; using it would test M_issuer / M_status on a value built from those variables

non_circular_checked.basis: force language, not the marker: R-86 "These become governing rulings effective immediately." (not governing before) and R-81 "“BATCH 7 IS RELEASED” DOES NOT HOLD"
R-86 has no marker and its value is not derived from its issuer; R-81 records that R-86's act operated: "(adoption act: R-86). THIS RULING IS GOVERNING." (operative = force per TASK)

unsupported_values.problem: rests on citation by R-89, itself PREPARED with no established force, and on 'left the PREPARED→ADOPTED mechanism in force', where 'in force' describes the mechanism, not R-88. A excludes R-60/R-66/R-72/R-76/R-79 as 'force presupposed, not stated'; R-88 is in the same position. If read as 'R-88 was adopted -> in force', the value is status-derived (circular).

strongest_alternative_readings.reading: R-81 as filed (status none stated) was NOT-IN-FORCE from the outset, because the Chief's determination is about authority that was lacking all along. Paired with R-86 (none stated, IN-FORCE) this would FALSIFY M_status.
strongest_alternative_readings.ruled_out: partly. R-81's final annotation says the ruling 'passed through a PREPARED state', and R-86 lists 'provenance corrected'. Both frame the unmarked filing as mis-recorded provenance of one PREPARED state, not as a separate 'none stated' state. The present-tense 'DOES NOT HOLD' does not state the as-filed force. Not ruled out beyond doubt.

strongest_alternative_readings.reading: Issuance by the Decision Authority is itself adoption: R-81 says the Session-1 mandate delegated 'CHAIRING AND PREPARATION, not adoption'. On this reading R-86's adopter is the Decision Authority, or UNK. Every known pair is then consistent and M_adopter is UNDETERMINED.
strongest_alternative_readings.ruled_out: no. The text never names an adopter of R-86, and R-81 shows that the register records adoptions in the adopted ruling's own row, which supports 'none'. But nothing excludes the merged reading.

strongest_alternative_readings.reading: R-86's force is the force of an adoption act, not a ruling's force, so its in_force is UNK. Then M_adopter is UNDETERMINED.
strongest_alternative_readings.ruled_out: largely. TASK counts 'operative' as force, and R-81 records R-86's act as having taken effect.

strongest_alternative_readings.reading: Use the rule-assigned status for R-95 (PREPARED) and derive NOT-IN-FORCE.
strongest_alternative_readings.ruled_out: procedurally yes. Both the status and the force would come from the issuer, which is circular, so this reading is inadmissible for testing.
